name: Injury Severity Score

version.label: ISS (Baker et al. 1974)
version.detail: Sum of squares of the highest AIS severity in the three most severely injured of six body regions. Any AIS 6 gives ISS 75. Range 0–75.

calculatorNotice.title: Requires AIS severities
calculatorNotice.message: Enter the highest AIS severity (0–6) for each region, from AIS coding. The AIS dictionary is licensed by AAAM and is not reproduced here.

resultStates.label: No injury recorded
resultStates.summary: No AIS-coded injury recorded at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Depends on complete injury identification and coding.

resultStates.label: ISS {total}
resultStates.summary: Below the ISS >15 threshold commonly used to define major trauma.

resultStates.label: ISS {total}: above 15
resultStates.summary: ISS >15 is commonly used to define major trauma.
resultStates.detail: Correlate with physiology and clinical status according to local trauma protocols.

resultStates.label: ISS 75
resultStates.summary: Maximum ISS (includes an AIS 6 injury, or three AIS 5 regions).
resultStates.detail: Correlate with the full clinical picture; ISS describes anatomy, not current physiology.

clinicalContext.text: The standard anatomical severity summary in trauma registries and research.

clinicalInsights.text: Only the single most severe injury in each region counts; multiple severe injuries in one region are under-represented (the New ISS addresses this).

limitations.text: Depends on accurate AIS coding, usually after full investigation.

limitations: Counts only one injury per body region.

confounders.effect: Severity codes differ between AIS versions.

guideSections.what: A 0–75 anatomical score derived from AIS severities in six body regions.
guideSections.whenToUse: Trauma registries, research and retrospective severity description.
guideSections.howToPerform: For each region, enter the highest AIS severity. Square the three highest and sum; any AIS 6 gives 75.
guideSections.clinicalContext: An anatomical descriptor, usually finalised after full assessment.

sources.citation: Baker SP, O'Neill B, Haddon W Jr, Long WB. The Injury Severity Score: a method for describing patients with multiple injuries and evaluating emergency care. J Trauma. 1974;14(3):187-196.

licensing.note: The Abbreviated Injury Scale dictionary is licensed by AAAM; only severity numbers are entered.
